title: Derived tensor of scalar models over a flat DVR sheaf algebra
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $A$ a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $A_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $R$ a commutative sheaf of $A_{\mathcal C}$-algebras flat over $A_{\mathcal C}$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P,Q$ put $P_R=R\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}\underline P$ and $Q_R=R\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}\underline Q$. In the unbounded module derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], $P_R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R$ has cohomology only in degrees $-1,0$, and each cohomology sheaf is isomorphic to $R\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}\underline N$ for a finitely presented scalar $A$-module $N$. Specifically for $r,s\ge1$, both $H^{-1}$ and $H^0$ of $(R/\pi^rR)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(R/\pi^sR)$ are $R/\pi^{\min(r,s)}R$. Tensors with the free summand $R$ leave the other module in degree zero.

source.place: paragraph (2), explicit DVR scalar-model calculation replacing the incorrect assertion that a finite free complex is a sum of shifts

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $A^m\xrightarrow{F}A^n\to P\to0$ using [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-matrix-smith-powers] to $F$. The invertible changes of bases identify its cokernel with the cokernel of the rectangular diagonal matrix: there is one $A/(\pi^{e_i})$ for each nonzero pivot and one $A$ for each unused target coordinate. Pivots with $e_i=0$ give zero summands and are discarded. Thus $P$ is a finite direct sum of copies of $A$ and $A/(\pi^r)$ with $r\ge1$. Apply the same argument to $Q$. Zero-dimensional presentations and empty sums are allowed.

source.place: paragraph (2), scalar finite-model tensor calculation; scalar Smith reduction using the existing DVR matrix theorem

proof.text: Write $T(M)=R\otimes_{A_{\mathcal C}}\underline M$. Constant realization preserves kernels and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-constant-exact]. Tensoring with $R$ is exact by the stated flatness hypothesis, whose definition is precisely exactness of this tensor functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Hence $T$ preserves kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums. These computations are also computations of $R$-modules: the induced $R$-action preserves each kernel and descends to each cokernel. The tensor unit map $r\otimes a\mapsto ar$, with inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$, gives $T(A)=R$. Applying $T$ to the scalar cokernel of multiplication by $\pi^r$ gives $T(A/(\pi^r))=R/\pi^rR$. The tensor maps here and below are the sheafified balanced maps of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3); Section 03EK, section-tensor-product

proof.text: For $r\ge1$, $A$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$ by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so $0\to A\xrightarrow{\pi^r}A\to A/(\pi^r)\to0$ is exact. Step 2 sends this to $0\to R\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R\to R/\pi^rR\to0$. Put $C_r=[R\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with quotient augmentation to $(R/\pi^rR)[0]$. Its kernel and cokernel show directly that this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. The free summand has resolution $R[0]$. Taking finite sums of these augmented complexes gives bounded finite free resolutions $C_P\to P_R[0]$ and $C_Q\to Q_R[0]$ for the decompositions in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; elementary domain cancellation and exact scalar extension from Step 2

proof.text: Tensoring with a finite free $R$-module is a finite coordinate sum of the identity functor, so every term of $C_P$ and $C_Q$ is flat. They are K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The K-flat comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] therefore identifies $P_R\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(C_P\otimes_R C_Q)$. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent] to the augmentation $C_Q\to Q_R[0]$ and the K-flat complex $C_P$. Interchanging the factors by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(p,q)$ gives the required orientation of that cited theorem. Thus the total complex maps by a quasi-isomorphism to $\operatorname{Tot}(C_P\otimes_R Q_R[0])$. Its degree $i$ is $C_P^i\otimes_R Q_R$ and its differential is $d_{C_P}\otimes1$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In particular a cyclic pair is computed by $[R/\pi^sR\xrightarrow{\pi^r}R/\pi^sR]$ in degrees $-1,0$.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding construction

proof.text: Compute the scalar kernel and cokernel of $\pi^r$ on $A/(\pi^s)$. If $r\ge s$, this map is zero, so both are $A/(\pi^s)$. If $r<s$, the cokernel is $A/(\pi^r)$, and multiplication by $\pi^{s-r}$ gives an isomorphism $A/(\pi^r)\to\ker(\pi^r:A/(\pi^s)\to A/(\pi^s))$. Indeed $\pi^r a=\pi^s b$ implies $a=\pi^{s-r}b$ by cancellation in the domain $A$, and $\pi^{s-r}b\in\pi^sA$ holds exactly when $b\in\pi^rA$, again by cancellation. Apply the exact functor $T$ of Step 2 to these kernel and cokernel identifications. The cyclic complex of Step 4 therefore has $H^{-1}\cong H^0\cong T(A/(\pi^{\min(r,s)}))=R/\pi^{\min(r,s)}R$, and has no other cohomology.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr; elementary quotient and cancellation calculation

proof.text: The finite coordinate maps $((x_i)_i,y)\mapsto(x_i\otimes y)_i$ and the inclusions of each coordinate give inverse balanced-tensor maps, so the complex in Step 4 is the finite sum of the complexes for the pairs of summands in Step 1 [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For a free left summand its complex is $Q_R[0]$ by $r\otimes q\mapsto rq$. For a cyclic left summand and a free right summand it is $C_r$, whose only cohomology is $R/\pi^rR$ in degree zero by Step 3. For two cyclic summands use Step 5. Kernels and cokernels of a finite block diagonal map are their coordinate sums, so cohomology is the finite sum of these computed sheaves. In degree $-1$ take the corresponding finite sum of $A/(\pi^{\min(r,s)})$; in degree $0$ take the scalar modules from all free/free, free/cyclic, cyclic/free and cyclic/cyclic pairs. These scalar modules are finitely presented: use one generator with relation $\pi^t$ for each cyclic term, one generator with no relation for each free term, and combine these finitely many presentations. Step 2 identifies each resulting sheaf with $T(N)$. Every block vanishes in degrees outside $[-1,0]$, proving every clause, including the free-summand assertion.
